---
title: "Organize UVP6 segmentations and traits"
author: "Patrick Pata"
date: "2025-11-25"
output: html_document
---

This file organizes the predictions of the CNN segmentation model for the lipid content of the individual images and appends the metadata of the morphological traits. The manual segmentation information used for model training is also loaded and compared with the CNN model ouputs. This file updates the deprecated UVP_CNN_model_evaluation.Rmd file. 

Whenever the CNN segmentation pipeline is updated, this file needs to be updated as well.

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```


# Load libraries and data
```{r}
library(tidyverse)

theme_set(theme_bw())
source("functions/lipid_pump_toolkit.R")

# Folder containing the predicted images and summary table file
# Note lipidfullness is based on pixels, *2 for pcrop, so remove here
fol <- "C:/Sync/UVP6_Data/lipid_predictions_20251123/"

```

# Curate the image data
```{r}
# 1. Load and select only the necessary columns
df.CNN.seg <- read.csv(paste0(fol, "new_predictions_uvp6_20251123.csv")) %>% 
  mutate(object_id = str_remove(filename, ".png")) %>% 
  select(object_id, 
         prosome_pixels = prosome_pixels_predicted,
         prosome_major = prosome_major_predicted,
         lipid_pixels = lipidpcrop_pixels_predicted,
         lipid_major = lipidpcrop_major_predicted) %>% 
  mutate(source = "CNN_segmentation")

# 2. Mark images found inside the bad images folder
# List file names of images inside the folder containing predicted images evaluated as bad segmentations
bad.images.files <- list.files("C:/Sync/UVP6_Data/lipid_predictions_20251123/bad_segmentations/")

df.CNN.seg <- df.CNN.seg %>% 
  mutate(is_bad_image = if_else(object_id %in% 
                                  str_remove(bad.images.files, "_overlapRGB.png"),
                                T,F)) %>% 
  relocate(object_id)

# 3. Switch the manually segmented images in. Only the images that have both prosome and lipid annotations.
# The output files of the model training
res.prosome <-  read.csv("C:/Users/patri/python_workspace/copepods-lipid-content/prediction_outputs/model_resnet34_prosomeUVP6_deamundp1_v2/prediction_prosome_uvp6_20251204.csv")

res.lipid.crop <-  read.csv("C:/Users/patri/python_workspace/copepods-lipid-content/prediction_outputs/model_resnet34_lipidcropUVP6_deamundp1_v2/prediction_lipids_uvp6_20251204.csv")

# Note that there are 2 images manually segmented that are not in the segmented images folder, because the taxa categorization changed 
df.manual <- left_join(res.prosome, res.lipid.crop,
                       by = join_by(filename)) %>% 
  mutate(object_id = str_remove(filename, ".png")) %>% 
  select(object_id, 
         prosome_pixels = prosome_pixels_annotated,
         prosome_major = prosome_major_annotated,
         lipid_pixels = lipid_pixels_annotated,
         lipid_major = lipid_major_annotated) %>%  
  mutate(source = "manual_segmentation") %>% 
  filter(!is.na(prosome_pixels) & !is.na(lipid_pixels)) %>% 
  mutate(is_bad_image = F)

df.CNN.seg <- df.CNN.seg %>% 
  filter(object_id %notin% df.manual$object_id) %>% 
  bind_rows(df.manual)


rm(bad.images.files, res.prosome, res.lipid.crop)
```

Add morphotraits data
```{r}
# Open morphological traits data
load("C:/Sync/UVP6_Data/Amund_UVP6_plankton_20251125.RData")
segmented.images <- df.CNN.seg %>% 
  left_join(Amund_UVP6, by = "object_id") %>% 
  select(-c(twilight.x, twilight.y)) %>% 
  rename(
    Major = object_major, Minor = object_minor, 
    Perim = object_perim., Feret = object_feret, 
    Area = object_area, Elongation = object_elongation,
    VerSym = object_symetriev, VerSym2 = object_symetrievc, 
    Circ = object_circ., Thickr = object_thickr, 
    MeanGrey = object_mean, MedGrey = object_median,
    HistGrey75 = object_histcum3, SdevGrey = object_stddev, 
    SkewGrey = object_skew, Fractal = object_fractal, 
    PerimFeret = object_perimferet, PerimMajor = object_perimmajor
  )

# Check if any missing metadata
segmented.images %>% 
  filter(is.na(Major)) %>% 
  nrow()

# All the copepods and their morphotraits 
# Note: currently includes unverified taxonomy
all.copepods.uvp6 <- Amund_UVP6 %>% 
  filter(taxagroup %in% c("Copepoda", "Copepoda-lipidsac")) %>% 
  # remove images predicted as dead/appendages/body parts, cyclopoids, harpacticoids, and other definitely not Calanus spp calanoids
  filter(object_annotation_category %notin% 
           c("antenna<Calanoida","antenna<Copepoda","with-eggs<Calanoida",
             "copepoda eggs","dead<Copepoda","part<Copepoda",
             "Cyclopoida","Harpacticoida","Heterorhabdus","Heterorhabdidae",
             "Paraeuchaeta","Metridia","female+eggs<Paraeuchaeta")) %>% 
  select(-c(twilight.x, twilight.y)) %>% 
  rename(
    Major = object_major, Minor = object_minor, 
    Perim = object_perim., Feret = object_feret, 
    Area = object_area, Elongation = object_elongation,
    VerSym = object_symetriev, VerSym2 = object_symetrievc, 
    Circ = object_circ., Thickr = object_thickr, 
    MeanGrey = object_mean, MedGrey = object_median,
    HistGrey75 = object_histcum3, SdevGrey = object_stddev, 
    SkewGrey = object_skew, Fractal = object_fractal, 
    PerimFeret = object_perimferet, PerimMajor = object_perimmajor
  ) %>% 
  mutate(major_length_mm = Major * 0.073) %>% 
  # Categorize Major length to 3-5 mm and >5 mm (most likely to be Calanus spp)
  mutate(major_length_cat = if_else(major_length_mm >= 3 &
                                      major_length_mm < 5,
                                    "size2", "size1"),
         major_length_cat = if_else(major_length_mm >= 5,
                                    "size3", major_length_cat)) %>% 
  # Of the images not segmented, only retain major lengths > 2mm
  filter(major_length_mm >= 2 | object_id %in% segmented.images$object_id)

rm(Amund_UVP6)
```

# Get size ranges of the data for training
This is used to guide the curation of the predictions.
Only consider images with both prosome and lipid manual segmentations.
```{r}
manual.segmented.images <- segmented.images %>% 
  filter(source == "manual_segmentation") %>% 
  select(object_id, Major, Minor, Feret, Area, 
         prosome.pixels = prosome_pixels, prosome.major = prosome_major, 
         lipid.pixels = lipid_pixels) 

sum.manual.seg <- manual.segmented.images %>% 
  select(-object_id) %>% 
  summarise(across(everything(), list(
    min = ~min(., na.rm = TRUE),
    max = ~max(., na.rm = TRUE),
    mean = ~mean(., na.rm = TRUE),
    median = ~median(., na.rm = TRUE),
    sd = ~sd(., na.rm = TRUE),
    n = ~sum(!is.na(.)) # Count of non-NA values
  ), .names = "{.col}_{.fn}")) %>% 
  pivot_longer(cols = everything(), names_to = "statistic", values_to = "value") %>%
  separate(statistic, into = c("column", "metric"), sep = "_") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = metric, values_from = value)
sum.manual.seg

# What is the relationship between the Ecotaxa area trait and the prosome pixels annotated area?
# The area as number of pixels identified by Ecotaxa is often larger than the prosome segmented.
# Interestingly, there are instances when the segmented prosome is larger than the area reported by Ecotaxa. Why?
ggplot(manual.segmented.images, aes(x = Area, y = prosome.pixels)) +
  geom_point(aes(color = lipid.pixels), alpha = 0.6) +
  scale_color_viridis_c(guide = F) +
  geom_abline() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", color = "red")
```


# Further curation of the automated lipid segmentations
```{r}

# *** EXCLUDE EXTRAPOLATIONS ***
# Many of these are also categorized as bad images
to_exclude_by_size <- segmented.images %>% 
  filter(source == "CNN_segmentation") %>% 
  # exclude all images smaller than the minimum size of the training data, also remove too small/large lipid and prosome pixel area!
  filter(prosome_major < filter(sum.manual.seg,
                                   column == "prosome.major")$min |
           prosome_major > filter(sum.manual.seg, 
                                   column == "prosome.major")$max |
           prosome_pixels < filter(sum.manual.seg, 
                                   column == "prosome.pixels")$min |
           prosome_pixels > filter(sum.manual.seg, 
                                   column == "prosome.pixels")$max |

           lipid_pixels < filter(sum.manual.seg, 
                                      column == "lipid.pixels")$min |
           lipid_pixels > filter(sum.manual.seg, 
                                      column == "lipid.pixels")$max)

segmented.images <- segmented.images %>% 
  mutate(exclude_by_size = if_else(object_id %in% to_exclude_by_size$object_id, 
                                         T,F))


# *** Apply data curations ***
# only manually segmented, not bad images, and not excluded by size
# This will exclude 744 images (733 bad, 11 more with extrapolated sizes)
segmented.images <- segmented.images %>% 
  filter(source == "manual_segmentation" |
           (is_bad_image == F & exclude_by_size == F)) %>% 
  select(-c(exclude_by_size, is_bad_image))

# Mark which images in the morpho traits dataframe could be used for the RF
all.copepods.uvp6 <- all.copepods.uvp6 %>% 
  mutate(traits_from_RF = if_else(object_id %in% segmented.images$object_id,
                                  F, T))
```

# ** Evaluate model training dataset **
* Refer to UVP_CNN_Model_evaluation.Rmd for plots and further analysis of the training model results. *

## Open file
Last model training done March 19, 2025

IoU: Area of intersection/Area of union (TP / (TP + FN + FP)) [Best for image segmentation]
Precision: TP / (TP + FP)
Recall: TP / (TP + FN)
F1score: 2 x (Precision x Recall) / (Precision + Recall) [Harmonic mean of precision and recall]
```{r}
# The output files of the model training
res.prosome <-  read.csv("C:/Users/patri/python_workspace/copepods-lipid-content/prediction_outputs/model_resnet34_prosomeUVP6_deamundp1_v2/prediction_prosome_uvp6_20251204.csv")

res.lipid.crop <-  read.csv("C:/Users/patri/python_workspace/copepods-lipid-content/prediction_outputs/model_resnet34_lipidcropUVP6_deamundp1_v2/prediction_lipids_uvp6_20251204.csv") 

# The metadata of the images used for model training
meta.lipid <- read.csv("C:/Users/patri/python_workspace/uvp6_de_amund23p1_lipid/metadata_lipid.csv") %>% 
  distinct(filename, .keep_all = TRUE)
meta.prosome <- read.csv("C:/Users/patri/python_workspace/uvp6_de_amund23p1_prosome/metadata_prosome.csv") %>% 
  distinct(filename, .keep_all = TRUE)

# Clean  the data frames
res.prosome <- res.prosome %>% 
  select(-c(directory)) %>%
  left_join(meta.prosome %>%
              select(filename, split, num_vertices),
            by = join_by(filename)) %>% 
  filter(!is.na(num_vertices)) %>% 
  mutate(object_id = str_remove(filename, ".png")) 

res.lipid.crop <- res.lipid.crop %>% 
  select(-c(directory, 
            lipid_mass_annotated, lipid_mass_predicted)) %>%
  left_join(meta.lipid %>%
              select(filename, split, num_vertices),
            by = join_by(filename)) %>% 
  filter(!is.na(num_vertices)) %>% 
  mutate(object_id = str_remove(filename, ".png")) 

# Summary of model training performance
res.prosome %>% 
  group_by(split) %>% 
  summarise(across(IoU:F1score, list(
    min = ~min(., na.rm = TRUE),
    max = ~max(., na.rm = TRUE),
    mean = ~mean(., na.rm = TRUE),
    median = ~median(., na.rm = TRUE),
    sd = ~sd(., na.rm = TRUE),
    n = ~sum(!is.na(.)) # Count of non-NA values
  ), .names = "{.col}_{.fn}"))

res.lipid.crop %>% 
  group_by(split) %>% 
  summarise(across(IoU:F1score, list(
    min = ~min(., na.rm = TRUE),
    max = ~max(., na.rm = TRUE),
    mean = ~mean(., na.rm = TRUE),
    median = ~median(., na.rm = TRUE),
    sd = ~sd(., na.rm = TRUE),
    n = ~sum(!is.na(.)) # Count of non-NA values
  ), .names = "{.col}_{.fn}"))
```

## Calculate and plot accuracy of waxester content
```{r}
res.lipid.crop <- res.lipid.crop %>% 
  mutate(lipid_area_mm2_annotated = lipid_pixels_annotated * 0.073 * 0.073,
         lipid_area_mm2_predicted = lipid_pixels_predicted * 0.073 * 0.073,
         waxester_mass_mg_annotated = 0.167 * (lipid_area_mm2_annotated ^ 1.42),
         waxester_mass_mg_predicted = 0.167 * (lipid_area_mm2_predicted ^ 1.42)) 


lipid.reg <- lm(waxester_mass_mg_annotated ~ waxester_mass_mg_predicted,
                data = res.lipid.crop)
(lipid.reg.sum <- summary(lipid.reg))
sqrt(mean(residuals(lipid.reg)^2)) # RMSE


ggplot(res.lipid.crop, aes(x = waxester_mass_mg_predicted,
                           y = waxester_mass_mg_annotated)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_abline() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", color = "pink")

```


# ** Extra evaluation scripts **

## Evaluate the predictions
### Check the effectiveness of some modelling choices
```{r}
# 1. Check probability of "predLipidSac" classification model
# ... should be all true, since most are validated except 2023 data.
# The classification model of lipid sac is not that good with cant segment at ~30% of images for the 2021 and 2024 data, and 45% of imags for the 2023 data. The model is probably not reliable overall since the 2021 and 20
df.CNN.seg %>% 
  # mutate(filename = paste0(object_id,".png")) %>% 
  mutate(year = if_else(grepl("2021", filename) == T,
                          "2021", "2024")) %>% 
  mutate(year = if_else(grepl("2023", filename) == T,
                          "2023", year)) %>% 
  group_by(year, predLipidSac) %>% 
  count() %>% 
  group_by(year) %>% 
  mutate(totalimgs = sum(n)) %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  mutate(percent = n/totalimgs*100)


# 2. Are lipid sac areas different between predicted classification?
# Usually the smaller images are predicted to "not have lipid sac" but maybe is biased by the training dataset being more larger images, as evidenced by the predicted prosome pixels.
ggplot(df.CNN.seg, aes(x = lipidpcrop_pixels_predicted)) +
  geom_density(aes(fill = predLipidSac), alpha = 0.6)

ggplot(df.CNN.seg, aes(x = prosome_major_predicted)) +
  geom_density(aes(fill = predLipidSac), alpha = 0.6)

# 3. How sure was the classification model about its predictions? Generally often more sure when predicting if there is a lipid sac.
ggplot( df.CNN.seg %>% 
          mutate(probab = if_else(predLipidSac == "lipid sac",
                                  prob_1, prob_0)),
        aes(x = predLipidSac, y = probab) ) +
  geom_violin() +
   geom_boxplot(width=0.1, color="pink", alpha=0.2) 

# 4. Compare values with and without prosome crop... seems like no effect, slightly higher for the prosome crop... at least make sures there are no 100% fullness
ggplot(df.CNN.seg, aes(x = lipid_pixels_predicted, y = lipidpcrop_pixels_predicted)) +
  geom_point(aes(color = prosome_pixels_predicted)) +
  scale_color_viridis_c() +
  geom_abline() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", color = "red")

ggplot(df.CNN.seg %>%
         pivot_longer(cols = c("lipid_pixels_predicted", "lipidpcrop_pixels_predicted"),
                      names_to = "prosome_crop", values_to = "pixels"),
       aes(x = pixels, fill = prosome_crop)) +
  geom_density(alpha = 0.6)

```

# Function to display the images
open_images <- function(filenames) {
  for (file in filenames) {
    if (file.exists(file)) {
      if (.Platform$OS.type == "windows") {
        shell.exec(file)  # Opens the image in the default viewer on Windows
      } else {
        system(paste("xdg-open", shQuote(file)), wait = FALSE)  # Linux
        system(paste("open", shQuote(file)), wait = FALSE)  # macOS
      }
    } else {
      message(paste("File not found:", file))
    }
  }
}

### True negatives - Not calanus
831 images were from 7 taxa (Metridia, Paraeuchaeta, Heterorhabdidae, Hyperiidea, Aglantha, Phyllodocida, and Salpida). Only Metridia develops a lipid sac similar to Calanus, but morphologically distinct. Generally, these taxa have a similar oval shape as a Calanus but have different morphological traits. 

If the segmentation models are very specific to Calanus, then all these images will be classified as "cant segment". But remember that the algorithm for training cant segment was based only on Calanus.
```{r}
df.not.calanus <- read.csv("C:/Sync/UVP6_Data/not_calanus_lipid_predictions_20251125/not_calanus_predictions_uvp6_20251125.csv")

# How many were classified as no lipid sac? 667 (78%) Correctly assigns cant segment
df.not.calanus %>% 
  group_by(predLipidSac) %>% 
  count()

# What taxa does it classify as with lipid sac? 
# Almost half of the Hyperiidae images (49%) are classified as Calanus with visible lipid sac. Surprisingly, second one is Aglantha at 26%. For the rest of the taxa, <20% are in this category.
df.not.calanus %>% 
  mutate(taxa = str_extract(directory,
                            "Metridia|Paraeuchaeta|Heterorhabdidae|Hyperiidea|Aglantha|Phyllodocida|Salpida")) %>% 
  group_by(taxa) %>% 
  mutate(totalimgs = n()) %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  filter(predLipidSac == "lipid sac") %>% 
  group_by(taxa, totalimgs) %>% 
  count() %>% 
  mutate(perc = n/totalimgs*100)

```
